answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a bridge escrow before it can earn, with reputation built only from work attested by unrelated peers. Forging many identities then costs real capital per identity, and at the nadir of trust - a brand-new, unattested account - the stake is the only backing it has. Like a willow bending under load, honest agents recover their stake over time, while clusters caught coordinating lose theirs, so fake identities become unprofitable at scale.
